However my Oregano is the only one of my three plants (the other two being Lemon Thyme and Lavender) that is having issues.

There are small brown bumps on the bottom of my matured leaves and it is spreading to the smaller sprouts, these spots begin to make yellow ringed burns on my leaves (and there are a little on the stems now too). My potted Oregano is having issues.

Does it look like this? If so bacteria may be and issue. I get nute burn sometimes that can look like that. You mentioned potting them up into terracota. Is the soil you used pre-treated with ferts and ad mixes? If so adding additional fertilizers may be causing burn. Trim the affected leaves back and try a light misting of the remaining plant. Good luck and thanks for posting.

Sounds like some type of ring spot virus. It's a common disease that affects many plants. There are also parasites, scale insects and fungus that can leave similar marks but your description makes me think it's ring spot.

The plant is probably a loss. But you could try pruning the affected areas and then just waiting to see what happens. Becareful to dispose of diseased clippings properly to avoid spreading the cooties. You can also just remove it from the planter and watch other plants closely to make sure they also don't get infected. Thyme and lavender tend to be hardy and rather disease resistant so they should be fine.

Personally I want desktop environments for PC.

What does that mean? This is my dream of the future.

I put on my VR headset. My PC is used via the environment I see through said headset. Not Augmented Reality (though I guess that could be an option if you want and have a VR headset with a forward facing camera). Virtual Reality.

I'm in a meadow. My bed is a fallen tree. My desk is a large flat rock. My programs are laid wherever I last left them, like items. Any other obstacles are other objects as general "details" to make it feel more alive. Maybe I hear the wind blowing, or birds chirping, or music playing, or wtv I wish.

To open a program (this would require a camera to view you), I tap on it (it'd have to be aware of my perspective, but it is because it's displaying that on my headset). It pops up and highlights. I snap my fingers and it flies up to me and consumes my whole range of vision. i.e. I just full screened it. I do wtv I do.

If I just double tap a program, it opens but as a literal window into the program. i.e. it stays away from me, but it hovers up, turns into it's open form, but it's a window I can physically walk around and see at angles. It isn't my focus essentially as I'm still technically in my desktop environment.

Full screening takes me out of that environment in that my focus is 100% wtv programs I have open. It could still be seen if only 70% of my view is taken up, but still.

If I need a keyboard, a virtual one might hover before me, or I might have something more creative (chest strapped? could a cool thing). Mouse is unnecessary though at this point as I have a hand and gestures are my different clicks (left, right, middle, etc). Regular tap is left click. Fist tap (or punch or wtv) is right click. Palm is middle click. You get the idea.

If I want to have two things open at once, I tap two programs then snap my fingers and they intelligently take up 50% of each side of my view. I can make a pinch with my fore finger and thumb to adjust sizes on edges of programs, say, if I want one 30% and one 70%. Maybe I can have presets for certain programs so they only take up wtv percentage, or they specifically always go in my top right or bottom left section of view.

If my OS supports it, I can use both hands at once, giving me two cursors and two focuses in essence. The cursors change shape based on what it currently understands my hands as being. i.e. any unclassified shape is default cursor. Fist is a fist. Palm is a palm. Pinch is a pinch, etc.

The environment thing could be an office. My programs could be sitting on a shelf in my office instead of strewn about a meadow. The limit on this is your imagination and the work people would have to put into creating these things.

Video games are what they are. I start the program, it drops me in to do what I do. Maybe for older games that don't "do" VR, it still appears on a window-like thing with my keyboard before me.

There are little things to figure out, like how it deals with it when you are turned away from the camera and it can't see your hands, but overall this is what I hope using a PC is like in the future.
